idiom_name: fixed recipient list: copy to the secondary channel, forward the original
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: interpose a component with two outputs on the channel. It consumes a message, publishes it unchanged to the primary receiver, and publishes an independent copy to the secondary channel that only the analysis component consumes. Copy, do not share: serialize or deep-clone the payload so the analyzer can neither mutate nor block the message the flow still owns. Deliver the copy out of band (separate worker, thread or queue) through a bounded buffer with an explicit overflow policy (drop oldest, overwrite, sample, or fall back to a synchronous send) and count the drops, because a tap whose buffer overflows silently is worse than no tap. Keep the wiring declarative and removable: inserting or removing the tap must be a configuration change, its failures must not propagate into the primary flow, and its liveness should be watched separately.
pitfalls: Calling the analyzer in-band turns observation into coupling: its latency and failures become the flow's.
Sharing the live message object with the analyzer lets the analyzer mutate primary state or block on it.
An unbounded secondary queue hides overload until memory runs out; the tap needs a bounded buffer and a drop policy.
